facts.text: Owatonna was founded in 1854 by settlers with English roots and named after the Dakota name for the Straight River, “Wakpá Owóthaŋna.”.
The Straight River dam, once powering a mill, was rebuilt to include a fish ladder, keeping the river alive for wildlife.
Kaplan's Woods, a hardwood preserve on the southern border, was originally owned by Josef Kaplan and now protects local biodiversity.
The Village of Yesteryear, a pioneer village opened in 1962, houses relocated historic buildings and museum exhibits about early Owatonna life.
In 1904, Federated Insurance, later known as Minnesota Implement Mutual Fire Insurance Company, was founded right here in Owatonna.
Owatonna’s historic downtown Main Street still echoes its 19th‑century roots, with preserved storefronts and the National Farmers’ Bank as a landmark.
